findings: [major] billing/reconcile.py:1 — live API credential hardcoded in source. PARTNER_API_KEY = "sk-live-4f8a9c2e..." commits a secret to a tracked file; it will exist in git history and every clone. Source from env/secret manager and rotate the key, since deleting the line does not un-leak it.

[major] billing/reconcile.py:7 — off-by-one drops the first ledger row. range(0, len(rows)) -> range(1, len(rows)) omits rows[0].amount, so balanced ledgers report mismatched and a ledger whose first row equals the discrepancy falsely reconciles. Locking assertion: reconcile_ledger_rows([Row(10.0), Row(20.0), Row(30.0)], expected_total=60.0) must be True; it returns False (sums 50.0). That assertion already exists as test_reconcile_matches_expected_total, so this diff breaks an untouched pre-existing test.

[major] billing/reconcile.py:14 — http_client is undefined in this module. The hunk header @@ -1,10 +1,24 @@ starts at pre-image line 1 and shows the file opening on the def, so no import block exists above and the diff adds none; fetch_partner_balance raises NameError on first call and has never been executed.

[major] billing/reconcile.py:12-18 — new public function fetch_partner_balance has no test coverage. test_reconcile.py still imports only reconcile_ledger_rows. Locking assertion: with a stubbed client, fetch_partner_balance("p_123") GETs .../partners/p_123/balance with an Authorization: Bearer header and returns the balance field, and a body lacking balance surfaces a typed error rather than a bare KeyError. Test-plan lens requested; orchestrator owns dispatch.

[minor] billing/test_reconcile.py:9-11 — the added test is insensitive to the changed behavior. With expected_total=999.0 the assertion holds whether the sum is 60.0 or 50.0, so it passes identically before and after the loop edit. Locking assertion: a case failing iff rows[0] is excluded, e.g. reconcile_ledger_rows([Row(5.0), Row(0.0)], expected_total=5.0) is True. Boundary cases around the 0.01 tolerance are also missing.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:6-8 — hand-rolled index accumulator reimplements the sum() built-in. sum(row.amount for row in rows) expresses this directly, and iterating the sequence rather than its indices removes the class of off-by-one that this diff introduced.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:6-9 — money handled as float with an absolute epsilon. Binary-float accumulation compared via abs(...) < 0.01 means the tolerance signifies something different at 10 rows than at 100,000. Decimal or integer minor units with exact comparison is the correct modeling. Partially pre-existing, but the accumulator lines are in the diff and response.json()["balance"] extends the assumption.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:12-18 — network I/O placed in a previously pure computation module. reconcile.py now needs network stubbing to test at all, and a reader looking for the partner API client will not look in the reconciler; this belongs in a billing client module with the key resolved there.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:14-18 — unguarded HTTP call: no timeout (a stalled service hangs the caller), no status check (4xx/5xx bodies surface as KeyError or a decode error), and partner_id interpolated unencoded into the URL path so a value containing / or .. reshapes the request.

[nitpick] billing/reconcile.py:6-9 — the hunk removes and re-adds four lines to change one, signalling an invisible whitespace or line-ending change that inflates the diff and obscures the substantive edit.

[nitpick] billing/test_reconcile.py:10 — Row is undefined in this file, with no import in the file or diff. Scope caveat: pre-existing pattern that this diff adds a second use of rather than introducing, so reported at reduced severity; an explicit import would still help if Row is a conftest fixture.

[nitpick] billing/test_reconcile.py hunk header — @@ -1,5 +1,9 @@ declares 5 pre-image and 9 post-image lines but 6 and 11 are rendered. Likely a fixture artifact, noted because a malformed header would make the patch unapplicable.
